Expat’s remote surgery medtech scores $92 million Series B for stroke care
Remedy Robotics just banked $92m to make remote stroke surgery real.
Simon Thomsen
Nov 17, 2026
2 min read
Share
0
Prefer Startup Daily
Remedy Robotics founder Dr David Bell. Image: supplied
Remedy Robotics, a San Francisco medtech treating stroke patients remotely, and cofounded by Perth-born doctor David Bell, has raised US$62 million (A$92m) in a Series B, backed by a range of Australian venture funds.
US venture firm DCVC led the round, with existing backers Blackbird, Tony Fadell’s Build Collective, Divergent Capital and KdT Ventures chipping in alongside the the University of California’s investment office, Skip Capital and super fund Hostplus as new investors.
Remedy previously raised US$35 million across its Seed and Series A rounds.
The fresh capital is for a clinical trial across the University of California’s network by a surgical robot designed to let specialists treat stroke patients hundreds of kilometres away. The medtech is seeking US Food and Drug Administration approval for procedures on the blood vessels supplying the brain. It also plans to place prototype robots with clinical partners, including the Australian Stroke Alliance.
Bell spent eight years in medicine, including cardiac surgery and air retrieval, before studying at Stanford, where he met his cofounder and CTO Jake Sganga. In 2021, the pair lined a garage in Venice Beach with lead, bought a second-hand X-ray machine and had a colleague in Berkeley operate their prototype remotely.
“This funding will allow our world-leading hardware, software, and machine learning teams to progress the N1 system towards clinical trials and potential FDA approval, while also developing additional features including full autonomy,” Sganga said.

The N1 robot lets a specialist at a console steer a catheter through a patient’s blood vessels. Its software uses machine learning to analyse scans, simulate procedures and match a 3D map of the vessels to live X-ray images. The team is also developing autonomous functions.
In August 2025, a Toronto neurosurgeon used the N1 to perform diagnostic angiograms on two patients at a hospital 6km away. A clinical team stayed with each patient while Pereira guided the catheter to check for narrowed or blocked vessels.
The N1 has yet to secure approval for routine clinical use anywhere. In Australia, Remedy and the Stroke Alliance want specialists in major cities to be able to remove a clot while the patient is still at their regional hospital.

articles.text:
Project Omega Raises $80 Million To Develop Nuclear Fuel Recycling Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 11:10 PM
Project Omega Raises $80 Million To Develop Nuclear Fuel Recycling Infrastructure
Project Omega has raised $80 million in Series A financing to develop nuclear fuel recycling infrastructure and long-duration power products. B Capital led the round, with participation from noa VC, 645 Ventures, and other investors focused on nuclear technology and national security. Existing investors Starship Ventures, Mantis Ventures, Decisive Point, Virta Ventures, Pace Ventures, Essential Capital, and Washington Harbour Partners also participated.
B Capital General Partner Jeff Johnson will join Project Omega’s board of directors.
The company is developing a non-aqueous pyroprocessing platform intended to recover useful materials from spent nuclear fuel. Its technology targets isotopes that can be used in long-duration power systems, reactor feedstock, and commercial, scientific, and medical applications.
Project Omega said the process does not separate pure plutonium and could reduce nuclear-waste volume by up to 90%.
Its initial products include radiovoltaic systems that convert the natural decay of radioisotopes directly into electricity. Potential applications include sensors, autonomous systems, communications infrastructure, spacecraft, undersea platforms, and equipment deployed in areas where battery replacement is difficult.
Project Omega has worked with Idaho National Laboratory through the ARPA-E CURIE program and demonstrated stable electrical current from strontium-90 at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. It has also developed radioisotope power systems through DARPA’s Rads to Watts program.
The financing will support a pilot facility for isotope recovery and feedstock production, construction of a nuclear fuel recycling facility, and further development and manufacturing of the company’s X Series expeditionary power systems.
Project Omega has offices in Newport, Rhode Island, and Hailey, Idaho, along with a laboratory in Fall River, Massachusetts.
KEY QUOTES:
America’s growing demand for reliable power is colliding with a nuclear fuel cycle that remains dependent on foreign supply and leaves enormous value stranded in used fuel. Project Omega’s technology has the potential to create multiple revenue streams from a largely untapped domestic resource, spanning long-duration power, reactor feedstock and strategic isotopes. We’re excited to support Staff Sheehan and his highly experienced team as they scale this platform and unlock economic potential across the nuclear value chain.
Jeff Johnson, General Partner and Global Head of Energy at B Capital
The country’s nuclear renaissance will not happen without the fuel. We have a domestic source for this, nearly 100,000 metric tons of used nuclear fuel, which is one of America’s largest untapped energy resources. We are building a vertically integrated strategy around an abundant domestic feedstock, with a non-aqueous recycling process that recovers useful isotopes, and products with clear strategic demand. That combination creates the potential for an entirely new nuclear innovation economy.
Stafford Sheehan, Founder and CEO of Project Omega

China Physical AI Roundup: UniX AI Raises $75M Pre-A, Plus TensorWorld, UBTech Order and Huawei CloudRobo
By Greg Bock · 17 November 2026 · 5 min read
Insider Brief
Chinese robotics companies attracted new funding and commercial orders across humanoids, robot components and physical AI, led by UniX AI’s 500 million yuan (about $75 million) Pre-A round.
TensorWorld raised more than $100 million across two early funding rounds, while robot-chip developer XiXuan Chuangzhi secured 500 million yuan (about $75 million) at a 4 billion yuan post-money valuation.
UBTech secured an order for 400 humanoid robots, Huawei Cloud released an open-source robot world model, and TARS and Robotera reported industrial and logistics deployments.
China ‘s robotics companies continue drawing fresh investment in humanoids , robot chips and training models, led by UniX AI’s 500 million yuan (about $75 million) Pre-A round. Other developments include a 400-unit UBTech humanoid order, Hesai’s third-quarter results and Huawei Cloud’s release of an open-source robot world model .
UniX AI
UniX AI , which makes wheeled humanoid robots for security, hotels and retail, has raised 500 million yuan (about $75 million) in a Pre-A round, Science and Technology Daily reported , citing the Suzhou company. Existing investors Xienuo and Yonghua added to their stakes. New backers include Greenland Group, a customer that joined as a strategic investor, along with Keli Sensing, HUST Ventures and others. UniX said it ships more than 100 robots a month, with peak monthly output above 300, and has batch orders from property groups, Certis and Inspur. Proceeds will fund algorithm research, product updates and wider use in property management, hotels and retail.
TensorWorld
TensorWorld, which was founded in July and is building physics-based foundation models that predict how objects move and interact, has raised more than $100 million across an angel round and an angel-plus round, according to a Starlink Capital post published by 36Kr . Cathay Capital and HongShan co-led the angel round, with IDG Capital, CDH VGC, Starlink Capital and Ant Group participating. Ant Group, Heyu Capital and Meituan Strategic co-led the later round.
XiXuan Chuangzhi
XiXuan Chuangzhi, a robot-chip company set up in May by UBTech, MetaX and Fenglong, closed a 500 million yuan (about $75 million) angel round at a 4 billion yuan (about $600 million) post-money valuation, China Securities Journal reported , citing a UBTech WeChat post. GGV Capital and Matrix Partners China co-led the round. Funds will go to chip and platform research, a software toolchain, hiring and joint testing with robot makers. XiXuan plans a development platform in 2027 and its first system-on-chip in 2028. MetaX is a listed chip designer.
UBTech
UBTech signed an agreement for Yongda Auto to buy 400 of its U1 Pro ultra-bionic humanoids, with delivery planned this year, NBD reported . NBD said it was UBTech’s first disclosed large order for that line. The robots will be used for product demonstrations, sales and customer service, and the partners plan a Shanghai showroom. The contract value was undisclosed. UBTech also signed a pact with Tianyi Telecom Terminal, a China Telecom unit, setting a three-year goal of more than 1 million home-companion robots and 100,000 ultra-bionic or wheeled humanoid terminals, IT Home reported . Those figures are market targets, not a firm purchase order.

articles.snippet: Elumelu Acquires Additional $70m Seplat Shares, Raises Stake to 22.05% Business Post Nigeria
articles.text:
Economy
Elumelu Acquires Additional $70m Seplat Shares, Raises Stake to 22.05%
Published 2 seconds ago
on 17/11/2026
By Adedapo Adesanya
By Adedapo Adesanya
Nigerian businessman, Mr Tony Elumelu, has acquired an additional $70 million stake in Seplat Energy Plc through his energy investment firm, Heirs Energies Limited, increasing its shareholding in the energy firm to 22.05 per cent.
The latest acquisition involved approximately 5.9 million shares, representing about one per cent of Seplat, Bloomberg reported, citing a spokesperson for Heirs Energies.
The transaction marks another increase in Mr Elumelu’s investment in the Nigerian energy company, following a similar acquisition in September and an initial purchase of a 20 per cent slice in December 2025.
In October, Heirs Energies acquired an additional six million shares, representing one per cent of Seplat, for approximately £53.22 million (about N94 billion), raising its shareholding to 21.07 per cent at the time.
The initial acquisition involved about 120.4 million shares purchased from French energy company Maurel & Prom for about $500 million.
The latest investment comes as Heirs Energies pursues plans to expand its operations and increase its stake in Seplat.
The company’s chief executive, Mr Osa Igiehon, said in an interview last month that increasing its holding in Seplat aligns with its growth strategy, which also includes raising oil production to 100,000 barrels per day by the end of the decade.
Meanwhile, Mr Elumelu is expected to assume the position of Chairman of Seplat on January 1, 2027, succeeding Mr Udoma Udo Udoma, who is due to retire from the organisation’s board on December 31, 2026.

articles.title: BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
articles.snippet:
BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $62.9 million for global support of energy automation and fuel-storage safety systems.
The post BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 10:39 AM
BAE Systems Receives Maximum $62.9 Million DLA Energy Automation Support Contract
BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services has received a fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum value of approximately $62.9 million for global support of energy automation and fuel-storage safety systems.
The Rockville, Maryland-based contractor will provide sustainment for operational technology, automatic tank gauging, independent alarm systems, and overfill-protection equipment.
The Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard are identified as customers under the contract. The broad customer group reflects the use of fuel-management and storage systems throughout military installations and operational locations.
The five-year contract includes no option periods and has a performance completion date of November 9, 2031. Its stated $62.9 million value is the maximum IDIQ ceiling rather than a guaranteed payment to BAE Systems.
The government will issue orders for required products or services over the performance period. The announcement does not identify an initial task order, guaranteed minimum, or specific amount obligated when the IDIQ contract was awarded.
Fiscal 2027 defense working capital funds are identified as the applicable appropriation. Future orders and obligations will depend on customer requirements, available funding, and the contract’s ordering procedures.
The procurement was competitive, with four responses received. The Defense Logistics Agency Contracting Services Office in Columbus, Ohio, is the contracting activity for contract SP4706-27-D-0002.
Automatic tank gauges help monitor fuel levels and related storage conditions. Independent alarms and overfill-protection equipment can reduce the risk of spills, equipment damage, environmental incidents, and operational interruptions.
Operational technology sustainment may include maintenance, technical support, configuration management, repair, replacement, and other services needed to keep these systems functioning. The government announcement does not provide a more detailed breakdown of individual tasks.
The contract gives multiple military services and the Coast Guard a common mechanism for obtaining global support. BAE Systems will be eligible to receive orders up to the ceiling during the five-year period, but actual contract revenue will depend on the number and value of orders placed.
